Hi Alice / Ethan —

Thanks — a few technical notes in advance of the deep-dive to give your network/security folks context. I'll plan to walk through these items on the call and can provide more granular config snippets after: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering
- PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint Service): no public egress required; we publish an NLB in our account and you create an interface endpoint in yours. Pros: no public IPs, simpler allowlist posture, better isolated. Cons: slightly higher per-GB cost and additional endpoint ENIs per AZ.
- VPC peering: lower per-GB cost and simpler routing for large volumes but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and routing table updates. Peering does not support transitive routing.

2) IP allowlist / static egress
- If you require IP allowlisting and choose peering, you can either: (a) allowlist a small set of static egress IPs we can allocate from a pool (we can provide a list), or (b) use an outbound NAT/Proxy on your side and only allowlist that IP.
- For PrivateLink, allowlisting is not required for customer egress; the interface endpoint traffic stays within AWS.

3) Ports & DNS
- Required: outbound HTTPS (443) from your subnet(s) to our endpoint(s) or via PrivateLink.
- DNS: if using PrivateLink we recommend enabling private DNS for the interface endpoint to map the Redwood hostnames to the interface ENIs.

4) Certificate/KMS
- TLS: standard server-side TLS is supported. If you need mTLS, we support client certs for Private deployments — we can discuss mutual TLS on the call.
- KMS: for Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments we offer customer-managed KMS integration for key encryption at rest; for Hosted API we maintain the keys but can enable additional controls.

5) Logging & audit
- We can provide request/response logs (configurable retention), token-level cost/latency telemetry, and audit logs for admin actions. We'll work with your security team to identify the exact artifacts for SOC2 evidence.

6) Suggested CIDR and routing checks to validate before the call:
- Confirm no CIDR overlap (your VPC vs Redwood endpoint VPCs).
- Please confirm the specific subnets (private subnets) you intend to use for the interface endpoint or peering.

I'll bring sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets for PrivateLink and example security group rules to the call. If helpful, we can also prepare a short runbook for provisioning (usually 1–3 weeks from signoff depending on procurement).
